points.description: States the difference in scope/accessibility: data members can be accessed by any member function of the class, whereas a local variable can only be used inside the one member function where it is defined.
points.partial_credit: Give about 2-3 marks if only one side is stated correctly (e.g. only that local variables exist/are usable only within their function, or only that data members are shared by the class's functions), or if the answer is vague about scope.

rubric.notes: Full marks for saying, in any wording, that data members are accessible across the class's member functions while local variables are only accessible within the function that declares them. Give part marks if only one half is clearly stated or the scope idea is vague. Give no marks for answers that discuss unrelated things (e.g. only syntax or types) without scope or accessibility. Extra remarks do not cost marks.
